name: Veterinary clinic ops (ezyVet alternative)
hypothesis: ezyVet (IDEXX-owned) has documented UX complaints; AI scribe + practice mgmt opening (US precedent: Shepherd, Instinct).

market_sizing.target_buyer: Practice owner / managing vet of an independent or small-group veterinary clinic (1–4 sites). Practice manager in larger corporates but corporate buyers tend to dictate from head office.
market_sizing.business_count_au: ~3,800 veterinary services businesses in AU (IBISWorld 2025). After consolidation by Greencross/Vetpartners/Apiam/National Veterinary Care, independent clinics number ~2,200–2,800 — this is the realistic ICP. ~15,000 registered vets work across these clinics.
market_sizing.business_count_global: US: ~32,000 vet clinics (AVMA). UK: ~5,000 practices. Canada: ~4,500. NZ: ~700. Combined English-speaking TAM ~45,000 clinics; ~50% addressable independents after corporate consolidation.
market_sizing.typical_size: 1–4 vets + 3–8 nurses/techs/admin. Annual revenue $700k (1-vet rural) to $4M+ (multi-vet metro hospital). Average revenue per clinic in AU ~$1.5M.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: ezyVet (IDEXX) — published starting at ~USD $150/mo, but real-world deployments commonly $300–$700+/mo per clinic including modules. Covetrus (RxWorks, Avimark, Impromed) — varies, typically $200–$600/mo. VisionVPM (AU/NZ) — quote-based, mid-tier. RoboVet — enterprise. Vetlinkpro/Vetbooks (AU-native legacy) — cheaper, ~$100–$300/mo. AI scribe add-ons (Talkatoo, ScribbleVet/Instinct, Shepherd TranscribeAI, CoVet, HappyDoc) — USD $50–$200/seat/mo.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: $250–$500/mo per clinic for a credible ezyVet alternative; multi-vet practices accustomed to $500–$1,000/mo on PMS+modules. AI scribe add-on $50–$100/seat/mo on top.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Inside sales + founder demos; clinical-vet champion drives most deals. Self-serve trial possible for solo/rural but mid-clinic buyers want demo + migration support.
pricing_reality.realistic_arpu_au: $300–$450/mo per clinic; multi-location lifts to $800–$1,500/mo per group. Heavy white-glove migration from ezyVet/RxWorks is the sales hurdle.
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Very high. Embedded payments (vet clinics process $1M+/yr GMV), pet insurance claim submission margin, IDEXX/Heska lab integration fees (one-time), pharmacy/online-store revshare, client communication (SMS, app), AI scribe seat add-ons, boarding/grooming modules. 2–3× ARPU expansion realistic; payments + insurance claims alone can double net revenue.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) ezyVet (NZ-built, IDEXX-owned since 2021) — strongest AU/NZ cloud PMS, criticised for complexity. 2) RxWorks (Covetrus, Brisbane-origin) — legacy AU stalwart, on-prem heritage now under Covetrus. 3) VisionVPM (AU/NZ) — established mid-market. 4) Vetlink Pro / Vetbooks — older AU desktop offerings. 5) Digitail — global cloud challenger, AI-native. 6) Instinct EMR (acquired ScribbleVet Jan 2026) — premium hospital tier. 7) Shepherd Veterinary (US) — AI-native, growing. 8) Provet Cloud (Nordic, expanding). 9) Greencross uses internal/Provet variants. The AU cloud-native independent segment is concentrated around ezyVet.
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: ezyVet founded 2006 (~20 years). RxWorks 25+ years. VisionVPM 20+ years. Classic UI-rot zone; ezyVet specifically widely critiqued for visual complexity and click-heavy workflows.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: Capterra and SoftwareAdvice ezyVet reviews repeatedly cite: "confusing, complicated", "learning nightmare", excessive clicks across coloured buttons, inventory/billing batch frustrations, and that the platform is powerful but onerous. r/Veterinary threads complain about ezyVet pricing creep post-IDEXX acquisition, IDEXX lab lock-in, and slow feature responsiveness. Some users say "EZYVET HAS NO REDEEMING FEATURES" (extreme but representative). RxWorks complaints centre on dated UI and Windows-only legacy. Cliniko-style polish does not exist for AU vets.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Instinct Science acquired ScribbleVet (Jan 2026) — vertical consolidation of AI scribe into PMS. Digitail continues raising and shipping AI features. Shepherd has been quietly growing in US independent segment. Covetrus took private (2022) and continues to roll up. ezyVet remains under IDEXX. AI scribe space (Talkatoo, HappyDoc, CoVet, VetGeni) is crowded and well-funded.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Very high. Vet AI scribe is one of the hottest 2025–2026 vertical-AI categories — search volume for "veterinary AI" grew >1,680% YoY 2024→2025. Instinct's ScribbleVet acquisition signals incumbents now own the AI-scribe vertical. Window for a pure AI-scribe wedge is closing (6–12 months); window for AI-native full PMS with AU integrations is still open ~12–18 months.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: 1) ezyVet's UX complexity creates daily friction — vets and nurses describe excess clicks, hidden menus, slow check-in. 2) Inventory management for drugs, vaccines, consumables across multiple suppliers (Provet, Lyppard, Apex) is painful and is where Manuva's inventory model genuinely fits. 3) S4/S8 controlled-drug register compliance is often paper or Excel alongside the PMS. 4) Clinical note time burden — vets spend 1–2 hrs/day on SOAP notes. 5) Pet insurance claim submission (PetSure / Bow Wow Meow etc.) is manual. 6) Multi-site reporting is weak.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: Vertical AI scribe trained on veterinary vocabulary + deep AU integrations (IDEXX/Heska lab, controlled-drug register, PetSure claims, Provet/Lyppard ordering, RACGP-equivalent VetCompass data) + workflow lock-in once medical records and drug register live in the system. Inventory + supplier depth is a defensible angle distinct from US AI-scribe entrants.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: IDEXX VetConnect Plus + Heska lab APIs (IDEXX may restrict for ezyVet-rival), Provet Cloud Order / Lyppard / Apex wholesale catalogs, Smartflow whiteboard (IDEXX-owned), Xero/MYOB, Tyro/Stripe, pet insurance claim APIs (PetSure), microchip registries (Central Animal Records, AAR), state controlled-drug regulators (varies by state), VetCompass-AU research data, Twilio.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Moderate-high. Clinical records and drug-register history in ezyVet are exportable but messy; clinics rarely migrate without forcing event. IDEXX may slow lab-integration access for competitors (key risk). Side-car AI-scribe play is the safer initial wedge; rip-and-replace is high-margin but slow.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: High. State-based controlled-drug (S4/S8) record-keeping regulations differ across states (NSW Poisons Reg, VIC DPCS, QLD Health, WA, SA, TAS each have variations). Veterinary Practitioners Board registration per state. Privacy obligations on pet-owner data. Pharmacy/dispensing regulations. Compounding and storage rules.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: 1) NSW SafeScript-equivalent for veterinary controlled drugs under ongoing reform. 2) VIC SafeScript expansion considerations. 3) Federal review of veterinary use of antimicrobials (AMR stewardship) creating reporting requirements. 4) State Vet Boards harmonising CPD/registration. 5) Pet insurance penetration rising (~30%+ of dogs/cats by 2026) — claim-submission integration becomes a competitive necessity. 6) AHPRA-style national veterinary registration is debated but not imminent. Drug-register reform is the strongest forcing function.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: High. Veterinary clinical workflow, drug-register rules, anesthesia/surgery whiteboarding, inventory by lot/expiry, and lab-result interpretation each require domain depth. Vet co-founder or paid clinical advisor essentially mandatory.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 10–16 months solo for credible MVP (scheduling + clinical notes + AI scribe + S4/S8 register + basic inventory + Tyro). Full ezyVet feature parity 24+ months.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: IDEXX/Heska lab integration may be gated by IDEXX (competitive dynamics), Smartflow integration similarly. AI scribe accuracy on veterinary terminology (species-specific, drug doses). State-by-state drug register rule engine. Multi-species clinical templates.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: High. Controlled-drug record-keeping, vet registration, and pharmacy/dispensing rules vary materially across NSW/VIC/QLD/WA/SA/TAS/NT/ACT — multiple rule engines required.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: AU hosting strongly expected (pet-owner PHI-equivalent + drug register audit). Supabase Sydney suitable.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: 1) AVA (Australian Veterinary Association) National Conference + state divisions — sub-$10k exhibitor. 2) Vet Practice Magazine + The Veterinarian publication sponsorships. 3) Vet Cong, AVBA (Business Association) events. 4) Facebook groups: Vet Tech Australia, Vets in Practice AU, etc. 5) University vet schools (UQ, Sydney, Melbourne, Murdoch, Adelaide, JCU) — new grads bring software preferences. 6) Provet/Lyppard rep referrals (visit every clinic). 7) Outbound LinkedIn to practice owners — clinic count manageable. SEO contested but "ezyVet alternative AU" rankable.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: 3–5 active: Australian Veterinary Association (AVA, with state divisions and special interest groups), Australian Veterinary Business Association (AVBA), state vet boards (regulatory rather than advocacy), Veterinary Nurses Council of Australia (VNCA), AVA-SIG groups (ASAVA small animal etc.).
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: 3–5: Vet Practice Magazine, The Veterinarian, Australian Veterinary Journal (AVJ — academic), AVA News, Veterinary Business (US but read in AU).
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: Approximately 15,000–30,000 combined members across active AU vet/vet-nurse Facebook groups (Vet Nurses Aus, Aussie Vets, Practice Owners group, etc.). Smaller than allied health but very engaged.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 5–8 per year (AVA Annual Conference, AVBA Practice Management Conference, AVA state branch conferences, AVNAT, Pan Pacific). Sub-$10k booths feasible at most.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: High. Clinic addresses publicly directoried (AVA find-a-vet, state vet board registers, Google Business). Practice owners are named on websites. ~2,500 independent clinics — fully reachable via outbound over 6–12 months.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Low without insider. Vets are a tight-knit, somewhat insider-trusting profession. An outsider builder will need a vet co-founder or strong clinical advisor to be credible — and ideally a few "vet champion" early customers. Manufacturing background is neutral but inventory/supplier credibility is a positive talking point.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Moderate. 5 reference customers achievable in 4–8 months but requires concierge-level onboarding and likely free 6-month pilots. Single influential vet champion (clinic owner with social presence) is force-multiplier.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Moderate. "ezyVet alternative" contested by Shepherd/Digitail/Instinct (US-skewed). "Veterinary software Australia" rankable. Long-tail ("S4 drug register software vet AU") winnable.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: High. IDEXX owns ezyVet AND VetConnect Plus lab API AND Smartflow — they are the gatekeeper to AU's dominant diagnostics ecosystem and have direct incentive to restrict access to competitors. Heska is now owned by Antech/Mars — a parallel gatekeeper. This is the biggest single risk factor; either you ship without lab integration (limited appeal) or you negotiate access (slow, uncertain) or you build alternative diagnostics workflows (manual upload). State drug registers are paper/portal-based, not API-gated.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: ~40–50%. Strongest reuse of the three items in this batch. Reusable: tenant/user/role, multi-location, suppliers (Provet/Lyppard map cleanly), products/SKUs with batch+expiry (drugs and vaccines map directly to Manuva's components-with-batch model), purchase orders, goods inwards, stock-on-hand by location, activity log, Xero connector. Non-reusable: appointment, clinical encounter, drug register, lab result.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Auth, tenant context, RLS, design system, server actions, Supabase migrations, supplier-filtered components (recent feature ports directly), batch/serial tracking, multi-location, goods inwards, Xero. The inventory + supplier work is a real head-start.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: None. Manuva targets manufacturers; vet clinics are a fresh GTM. No bundle play, but the inventory story is genuinely transferable as a credibility wedge.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Medium — higher than the other two healthcare items. Vet inventory (drugs/vaccines with batch+expiry, multi-supplier ordering, par-level reordering, goods-inwards reconciliation, controlled-substance audit trail) is operationally close to manufacturing components/BOM workflows. Founder can pitch "we know inventory" credibly.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 12–18 months. The PMS shell + AI scribe is replicable. Real moat is IDEXX-equivalent lab integrations, state-by-state drug-register engine, and pet-insurance claim depth — these take 12+ months and are gatekeepered.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Healthy ~75–80% with AI scribe metered. Heavier onboarding cost than allied health (data migration from ezyVet/RxWorks is non-trivial) — bake in $1k–$3k setup fee. SMS/comms pass-through. Lab-integration build is fixed cost amortised across customers.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Yes. Group practices are common (2–6 sites); independent corporate-lite groups exist. Per-clinic pricing scales naturally and ARPU per logo is higher than allied health.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Low once drug register + clinical history are inside; clinic owners are stable and switching cost is high. Bigger risk is corporate-acquisition events (Vetpartners/Greencross acquires customer → forces migration to corporate-mandated PMS).
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: At $400/mo ARPU: ~210 clinics for $1M ARR. With ~2,500 independent ICP, 8–10% market share gets there. Aggressive but achievable with focused GTM; expansion to NZ ($700 clinics) and UK ($5k clinics) extends runway materially.
